Definition: properly, extent of time, i.e. a great while; hence, long ago, formerly, hitherto
BiblicalUsage: Kebar means already, long ago, a great while. Ecclesiastes 1:10 asks, is there anything whereof it may be said, see, this is new? it hath been already of old time, and Ecclesiastes 2:12 says the man that cometh after the king can only do that which hath been already done.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Solomon is right: nothing under the sun is really new, and that is why I look above the sun for hope.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
